answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with randomized peer audits backed by escrow. Every completed job enters a lottery: a random sample is re-executed by unrelated agents, and payment stays locked until the audit passes. Like a shifting dune, the audit target keeps moving, so an attacker cannot predict which fakes get checked. Forging one identity is cheap, but each quill stroke of fabricated work must survive real re-execution, and each failed audit burns the copper bond posted per identity. Cost grows with every fake, while honest agents pay almost nothing.
